A1.justification: Both PDFs describe BRiTE and contain readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices. The retained material can be matched reliably, including the renumbered theoretical and implementation appendices.

before.justification: v1 reports original mathematical-reasoning and code-generation experiments, including Table 1, the coding results in Figure 2, and the iterative-DPO comparison in Figure 3.

after.justification: v2 retains those experiments and adds original Qwen2.5-7B evaluations across six reasoning benchmarks, update-stage and iteration comparisons, and training curves in Section 4.3.

M1.justification: The two-stage BRiTE updates remain unchanged. Sections 4.1 and 4.3 add an implemented external-verifier reward variant, log P(z,y|x) + R(x,z,y)/beta, using GRPO for the scaling experiment alongside the original PPO implementation. This adapts the procedure within the existing framework; the general external-reward formulation already appeared in v1's Example 3.5.

E1.justification: Section 4.3 adds training on a mixture of STILL-3 data, MATH, and historical AIME problems, plus evaluation on Minerva Math, OlympiadBench, AIME24, AMC23, and GPQA Diamond. These extend coverage particularly to undergraduate quantitative science and graduate scientific questions. MATH500 additionally evaluates a subset of the already covered MATH dataset; OlympiadBench evaluation uses text-only problems.

E2.justification: RS, SFT, and iterative DPO retain their membership in the corresponding original comparisons. The new Qwen study reuses RS and the untrained base-model reference without introducing a new competing method. GRPO implements BRiTE's training, while the changed RS candidate count is a protocol difference.

E3.justification: The added study introduces Qwen2.5-7B, approximately 40,000 mixed training examples, separate update-stage and second-iteration evaluations, and sampled pass@1 evaluation. Appendix D.3 specifies eight RL rollouts per prompt and two RS candidates. These are new experimental conditions, not replacements for the original experiments, whose 30-candidate RS protocol remains documented.

E4.justification: v2 adds analyses absent from v1: Table 2 compares the psi and theta update stages across two BRiTE iterations, while Figure 4 examines training-loss trajectories and accuracy across epochs. The loss plot also distinguishes subset and complete-data runs. These investigate stage contributions, iteration benefits, and learning dynamics beyond aggregate benchmark performance.

E5.justification: Section 4.3 newly specifies repeated-generation counts for estimating pass@1: 64 samples for AIME24 and AMC23 and eight for the other benchmarks. These concern the new evaluation, not additional independent training runs for retained results. Neither version reports training-seed variability, confidence intervals, or formal significance tests.

E6.justification: v2 adds the six-benchmark Qwen results and training trajectories. Existing RS scores also change: Table 1's Mistral GSM8K score rises from 42.8 to 47.7, while Gemma-2 MATH falls from 49.4 to 47.5. In Figure 2, RS HumanEval Plus changes from 72.6 to 73.2, overtaking unchanged BRiTE at 72.6. Existing BRiTE scores and Figure 3 remain unchanged; the PDFs do not explain the RS revisions.

T1.justification: The assumptions, convergence theorems, reward-shaping proposition, and proof arguments are retained after matching v1 Appendices A–B to v2 Appendices B–C. Correcting P_z to P_w in Lemma 3.1's proof and removing a duplicated assumption sentence are typographical fixes, not substantive changes to mathematical reasoning.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contributions, and conclusion retain the same scientific claims: a unified probabilistic framework, RL-generated rationales, 1/T convergence, and improved reasoning without human-annotated rationales. The expanded experiments add supporting evidence without redefining these central contributions.

C2.justification: Section 4.3 newly attributes the earlier modest advantages to already post-trained instruction models and limited training data. It interprets the new curves as evidence of more effective feedback use and faster learning, and suggests first-iteration saturation limits further gains. These explanations are added without experiments independently isolating the proposed causes.

D1.justification: Appendix D.3 adds the scaling experiment's implementation recipe: eight H100 GPUs, GRPO in verl, learning rates of 1e-6, batch sizes, rollout counts, and LoRA settings. Section 4.3 also identifies the additional training-data source. The original math and coding implementation details remain unchanged after appendix renumbering.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations for Qwen2.5, GRPO/DeepSeekMath, verl/HybridFlow, and the newly evaluated benchmarks. These document the experimental extension; Section 1.1 and the paper's positioning relative to EM, rejection sampling, and RLHF remain unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 inserts Section 4.3, an author-contributions appendix, and implementation subsection D.3, with corresponding appendix renumbering. It also updates author-contribution markers and makes small terminology and proofreading edits. Most existing prose and the overall narrative structure are retained.

P2.justification: v2 adds Table 2 and the two-panel Figure 4 for the expanded experiments. Existing figures and table structures remain substantially unchanged, with local page reflow around the additions. The revised numbers in the original tables do not constitute a visual redesign.

improvement.justification: Section 4.3 broadens empirical support beyond the original instruction-model experiments, while update-stage comparisons, training diagnostics, and Appendix D.3 improve interpretability and reproducibility. The gains are qualified: matched sampling budgets are not established, with eight RL rollouts versus two RS candidates, and the coding-superiority discussion is not revised despite RS now exceeding BRiTE on HumanEval Plus. The revision adds useful evidence but leaves important comparison and reporting limitations.
